    AI Overview
    The historic Artemis II mission is scheduled to launch from Kennedy Space Center’s Pad 39B on Wednesday, April 1, 2026, at 6:24 p.m. ET, marking the first crewed flight around the Moon in over 53 years. Following this, a SpaceX Falcon 9 is scheduled for a Starlink mission on Thursday, April 2, 2026, at 7:52 a.m. ET. 
    Upcoming Launches 
    • Mission: NASA Artemis II
      • Time: 6:24 p.m. ET (April 1, 2026)
      • Location: Launch Pad 39B, Kennedy Space Center
      • Details: Four astronauts will perform a 10-day flight around the Moon.
    • Mission: SpaceX Starlink 10-58
      • Time: 7:52 a.m. – 11:52 p.m. ET (April 2, 2026)
      • Location: Launch Complex 40, Cape Canaveral Space Force Station
    • Mission: ULA Amazon Leo 5
      • Time: TBD (Postponed from April 1)
      • Location: Launch Complex 41, Cape Canaveral Space Force Station
    • Mission: SpaceX/Northrop Grumman CRS-24
      • Time: April 8, 2026
      • Location: Launch Complex 40, Cape Canaveral Space Force Station 
    Viewing Information 
    • Live Coverage: FLORIDA TODAY Space Team offers coverage starting hours before liftoff.
    • Official Viewing: The Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex offers ticketed viewing locations, including the Gantry at LC-39.
    • Local Viewing: Public spots include Jetty Park or beaches along the Space Coast. 
    All times are subject to change based on weather or technical issues.

      AI Overview
      To watch a Cape Canaveral launch in 2026, stream live via SpaceX.com, NASA+, or YouTube for full coverage, starting about 5–15 minutes before liftoff. For in-person viewing, top spots include Jetty Park, Cocoa Beach, Playalinda Beach, or Space View Park in Titusville. 
      Key Tips for Launch Viewing:
      • Best Viewing Spots:
        • North Launches (SLC-40/41): Playalinda Beach, Max Brewer Bridge, Space View Park. 
        • South Launches (SLC-37B/36/46): Jetty Park, Cocoa Beach, Cape Canaveral. 
      • Official Experiences:
        Book tickets at the Kennedy Space Center Visitor Complex for viewing near the action. 
      • Live Coverage:
        Watch SpaceX Falcon/Starlink launches on their website/X app, and NASA/ULA launches on NASA's YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@NASA) or [Spaceflight Now. 
      • Apps & Tools:
        Use the "Space Coast Launches" app for schedules, notifications, and location tracking. 
      • Important Info:
        Check launch dates on floridatoday.com/space.

        Rocket Types. What are the different types of rockets launched from Cape Canaveral?
        About this result
        Feedback
        An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
        AI Overview
        Cape Canaveral (Space Force Station and Kennedy Space Center) primarily launches SpaceX's Falcon 9 (satellite/crew transport) and Falcon Heavy (heavy payload) rockets, alongside United Launch Alliance's (ULA) Atlas V (national security) and the new Vulcan Centaur. Historically, it supported Titan, Delta II/IV, and Saturn rockets. 
        Key Rocket Types & Usage Examples (2024-2026):
        • Falcon 9 (SpaceX):
          The most frequently launched rocket, used for Starlink internet satellites, Falcon 9-NASA Crew-8/CRS-30 resupply missions, lunar lander deliveries (Intuitive Machines IM-1), and GPS satellites. 
        • Falcon Heavy (SpaceX):
          Designed for heavy payloads, used for interplanetary missions and large satellites like GOES-U. 
        • Vulcan Centaur (ULA):
          A new heavy-lift vehicle used for national security missions and commercial cargo (Vulcan Cert-1). 
        • Atlas V (ULA):
          A versatile, legacy rocket used for launching satellites and spacecraft like the Boeing Starliner. 
        Synonyms/Related Terms:
        • Launch Vehicles: Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy, Vulcan, Atlas V, Delta IV Heavy. 
        • Operators: SpaceX, ULA (United Launch Alliance), NASA, Space Force. 
        • Payload Types: Satellites, Crew Capsule (Dragon/Starliner), Spacecraft, Probes. 
        Historical Rockets: 
        • Titan IV B/IIIC: Heavy-lift military rockets.
        • Delta II 7920 10c/Delta IV Heavy: Medium to heavy lifters.
        • Saturn 1: Apollo-era rockets.
        These rockets launch from specific pads, such as Complex 40 (Falcon 9) or Complex 41 (Atlas V/Vulcan).

          Missions. What are the missions of Cape Canaveral launches?
          About this result
          Feedback
          An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
          AI Overview
          Cape Canaveral launches primarily focus on high-frequency SpaceX Starlink satellite deployments, crewed lunar missions like Artemis II, and scientific or defense payloads. Key 2026 missions include launching astronauts around the Moon and expanding internet constellations, with high-frequency launches using vehicles like Falcon 9 and Starship. 
          Key Mission Examples & Types (As of March/April 2026):
          • Artemis II (Crewed Moon Orbit):
            A historic crewed mission launching early April 2026 to orbit the Moon. 
          • SpaceX Starlink Missions:
            High-frequency launches (e.g., March 30, April 2) to expand the internet satellite constellation. 
          • Commercial Lunar Payloads:
            Missions such as those planned by Blue Origin or other private companies aiming for lunar surface exploration. 
          • Transporter Missions:
            Dedicated small-satellite ride-share missions (e.g., Transporter-16) to low-Earth orbit. 
          Synonyms for Cape Canaveral Launch Mission Types:
          • Space Flights: Orbital launches, space missions, rocket launches.
          • Satellite Deployments: Starlink missions, commercial launches, orbital insertion missions.
          • Space Exploration: Artemis missions, lunar missions, crewed flights, space station resupply missions.
          These launches predominantly occur from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station (SLC-40) and nearby Kennedy Space Center.
